描述_ZN: Ink and Bamboo, Ming dynasty, Wang Sash, ink and wash brush on paper, 113.8 cm in length and 51.3 cm in width.　　The painting depicts three bamboo plants with ink brushstrokes, the tips of the poles standing up and the branches and leaves swaying, with a dashing and elegant appearance; the branches are moist and the tips of the leaves are slightly drooping, with the appearance of rain and dew. Wang Sash is famous for his paintings of bamboo and rocks in landscapes, and his paintings of bamboo are especially "pioneering" in the Ming Dynasty. This painting is an inheritance from the Yuan Dynasty, but with new ideas. The bamboo leaves are drawn with round and strong strokes, and the branches are drawn with a straight and wide brush, and the leaves are naturally skimmed out with the hand to reflect the front and side of the leaves and the back, as well as the look of the leaves. The dryness and intensity of the ink and the size and sparseness of the brushstrokes are used to express the sense of space and three-dimensionality of the bamboo clusters. The brushwork is skillful and simple, and the shapes are vivid and realistic, with a refreshing charm.　　According to legend, there is a story about Wang Sash's bamboo painting. When he was in Beijing, he heard the beautiful sound of the xiao at night, so he painted a piece of bamboo on his own initiative and visited the xiao player the next day to present it to him in person. He was a big businessman and was so happy to see this that he immediately sent Wang Sash a generous gift and asked him to paint another one. Wang Sash laughed and said, "I visit for the sound of the xiao, you to xiao material, you vulgar son also." So he tore up the previous painting and returned the gift. This kind of arrogant and solitary character is naturally revealed in Wang Sash's ink and bamboo paintings, which have become a reflection of his personality.　　This painting is inscribed with the following inscription: "Written by Wang Fang on the 9th day of the xinsi year of the year of the Chinese calendar and sent to the Zen master outside of the dust." Inscription at the bottom: "Meng Duan". On the edge of the frame is an inscription by Wu Hufan: "Xinsi is the third year of Jianwen, when the man of Kowloon Mountain was forty years old. There is a plucked mark on the word Xin, which is frowned upon after the Yongle pacification." Accordingly, the word Xin above the missing should be "Jianwen" two words, after the reform of Yongle, collectors taboo, for fear of unpredictable disasters, so dig out. Political turmoil every time involved in the artwork, this one example. Fortunately, not much digging, no major damage to the painting. In Hongwu, Wang Sash was implicated in the incident and relegated to Datong, Shanxi, and was released to Nanjing in the first year of Jianwen's reign. The "History of Silent Poetry" states that Wang Sash tried to "travel to Taihang, out of Yanmen, and between Jin and Dai Dynasties, and always visited the scenic spots, and wandered about with emotion and hunger for the past. A time to hear, people admire his name, vying to extend to the, and view his appearance magnificent shore, argument excelsior, benefit more respect." It is clear that although Wang Sash was relegated, he became more experienced and his literary skills grew higher.　　Wang Sash used the painting of bamboo to express his feelings, expressing his praise for his personality of being out of the ordinary and not conforming to the vulgar and dirty people, so he inscribed it to his friend as "Qing offerings". Wang Yingxiang of the Qing dynasty inscribed a poem in the upper left corner of this panel: "I miss the immortals of the Jade Hall in the sky, and I have been decorating Sorry Row for several years. Looking back at my homeland, I have not yet returned, and my dreaming soul should be around the bamboo stream." It is thought that Wang Sash made this picture to express his nostalgia for his hometown by writing about bamboo.　　In the hall of poetry, there is a poem by Shao Bao of the Ming Dynasty with the following title: "The leaves of the bamboo are so beautiful that it is difficult to paint them. Who believes that the Chinese calligraphy had put the brush, a piece of time line all Chu River thousand." Wang Sash's attainments in bamboo painting were highly praised. The so-called "Zhongshu" in the poem refers to Wang Sash, who was the official "Zhongshu sheriff", but when Wang Sash became the official Zhongshu sheriff, it was already the tenth year of Yongle (1412), which was more than ten years after this picture was made.
